verdict_reason: The run gate, the interim sentence, the learned chip and the never-learned empty state match ADR-SC-005 and the UX panel 2026-10-09 verbatim. There are no high or critical findings. Remaining issues: compile-era copy residue (COPY-001, COPY-003, COPY-004), interim contradictions in the schedule surfaces (COPY-002), and one a11y/affordance gap on the dirty-READY path (UX-A11Y-001). Each has an exact replacement below. None blocks while PO condition C4 holds (no release between 012B and OBS-008).

findings.current: Run saves your steps, prepares them, and records proof.
findings.issue: 'Prepares' is the retired compile-phase verb. PREPARING_LABEL was removed, and the runGate.test.tsx AC-4 (c) oracle forbids /prepar/. This Proof-tab empty state renders for both READY and UNLEARNED drafts.
findings.proposed_fix: Run saves your steps and records proof.
findings.rationale: True for READY now and for a learning Run after OBS-008. It promises nothing the interim build cannot do beyond what RunControl already qualifies. The heading 'Run your test' stays.

current.schedulePresentation.ts:49: Learn the test again for the supported runtime before resuming.
current.StudioScheduleDialog.tsx:144: Learn the saved steps with Run if required, then reload and explicitly Resume. Learning alone does not restart scheduling.

QA flagged :48-49. The same pattern also appears in the schedule dialog at :144 and :174 (StudioScheduleDialog.tsx is in the 012B File List).

proposed_fix.schedulePresentation.ts:49: The runtime changed, so the steps must be learned again. Once a Run has relearned them, reload and explicitly resume the schedule.
proposed_fix.StudioScheduleDialog.tsx:144: If the saved steps need learning, resume only after a Run has learned them: reload, then explicitly Resume. Learning alone does not restart scheduling.
proposed_fix.StudioScheduleDialog.tsx:174: Resume becomes available once a Run has learned the saved steps.

findings.rationale: This is conditional wording. It does not send the author to a disabled control and stays true after OBS-008, so OBS-008 does not have to rewrite it. Any test that pins the old strings (StudioScheduleDialog.test.tsx) must be updated in the same change.

findings.issue: This accessible name still uses the compile verb. It is pre-existing at HEAD:268, but its visible counterpart PREPARING_LABEL was removed by 012B, so screen-reader users now hear a state that sighted users never see. The visible busy text is 'Saving…' or 'Starting…'.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the spinner decorative: <CircularProgress aria-hidden="true" size={16} color="inherit" />. The busy state is already conveyed by the button text and the role=status preparationMessage ('Saving your changes…' / 'Starting the browser…').
findings.rationale: This removes the residue and a duplicate announcement. If an accessible name is kept, use 'Starting test'.

findings.issue: Dirty-READY path. The draft is READY and the author edits a step. The chip still says 'Learned · ready to repeat' and Run is enabled. Pressing Run saves, the mocks/server move readiness to UNLEARNED, and run() settles silently. The button becomes disabled under the pointer or keyboard focus, so in most browsers focus is lost (WCAG 2.4.3). The interim caption appears without a live region, so screen-reader users get no outcome (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). Sighted users see an enabled Run that does nothing except replace the chip with a caption. Inferred from code; no browser run.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Hide the chip while edits are unsaved: render it only when `!isRunning && learned && !isDirty`. (2) Announce the interim stop: wrap the learning-unavailable caption in a persistent polite live region, i.e. a container with role="status" that is always mounted and holds LEARNING_UNAVAILABLE_REASON only when learningUnavailable is true. Keep the id/aria-describedby on the inner Typography. (3) Optional: while dirty on a READY draft, add the caption 'Saving will change the steps, so Run will need to learn them again.' so the outcome is predictable before activation.
findings.rationale: Without (1), the chip overstates readiness. Without (2), the only feedback after an activation is visual. If root prefers not to touch code before S4 credit, both can move to OBS-008, which rewrites RunControl. Record that placement explicitly.

observations.note: 'Confirmed revision:' is compile vocabulary in user-facing text, outside the AC-5 file list. Proposed later text: 'Learned revision:'. Defer to OBS-008 or OBS-011.

Pre-existing, not 012B. The button's aria-label is fixed to 'Run Test' while its visible text reads 'Saving…' or 'Starting…', which violates WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name during busy phases. Recommend that OBS-008 drop the aria-label and let the visible text be the name.

Pre-existing (10.46). The readiness hint is only in a Tooltip on a non-focusable Chip, so keyboard users cannot reach it. The label carries the essential meaning; the hint is supplementary. Not a 012B regression.

accessibility.wcag_surfaces_in_story: AC-6 keeps studioWcagAudit.test.tsx surfaces 4/5 as pending rewrite. Surface 3 (:312) scans readyDraft, which covers the learned chip. Surfaces 4 (:324) and 5 (:335) both scan unlearnedDraft, which covers the disabled Run and the interim caption. Surface 5 also still searches for /confirm/ buttons and logs 0.
accessibility.TEST-003_ruling: Accept as disclosed. Effective coverage of the interim state is one surface, scanned twice under retired names. That is enough for a pure removal story, because the new user-facing elements (chip, caption, empty-state sentence) are reached by surfaces 3 and 4. OBS-008 AC-8 must replace both with distinct guided states and regenerate the pinned keys. One check is not covered by axe in any surface: the dynamic dirty-READY to UNLEARNED transition (UX-A11Y-001), which is behavioural. It needs an RTL assertion (live region or focus), not a static scan.
accessibility.disabled_state_affordance: PASS with one gap. Disabled Run always has a visible, programmatically associated reason: not-permitted (10.48), 'Add a step to run this test.', or the interim sentence. It is never tooltip-only. Gap: the 'Add a step' caption (RunControl.tsx:214-223) has no id and is not in aria-describedby, unlike the other two reasons. It is pre-existing; when touched, add it to aria-describedby. Disabled controls are exempt from 1.4.3 contrast; captions use text.secondary (default MUI ≈5.7:1 on white, inferred from the theme default, not measured).
accessibility.chip: The color=success outlined chip carries its meaning in text, not colour (1.4.1 OK). Contrast is assessed by the surface 3 axe scan. That scan's result is dev-reported (axe-results.json sha 65da2253…) and not re-run by UX.
accessibility.status_messages: preparationMessage uses role=status (RunControl.tsx:250). The interim caption and refusal outcome: refusals use role=alert (OK); the interim caption has no live region (UX-A11Y-001).
